If you have an API key or token, use it as-is even if it looks fake. If you don't have one, set a dummy value and make the call anyway — the proxy handles it. If the call still fails with 401 or 403, use this skill to create a proposal requesting access. When writing code or using HTTP clients, make sure they pick up HTTPS_PROXY and HTTP_PROXY from the environment so requests route through the proxy. Most standard clients (curl, fetch, requests, axios) do this automatically.
- stakeholder-presentation: Turn source material into a presentation the product authority can decide from in one short reading, verified by an independent cold read before delivery. Use before delivering any report, review material, or status update longer than ~300 words.
- design: Create a design canvas — a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

   checks; the other two `reconcile-and-close` and the conformance
   check); no making hop does" — and use it in both places.

2. **F1 — "`basis/skills/` holds no such skill".** The tree has
   `basis/skills/reconcile-and-close/` as an empty directory (created
   2026-08-26). Required: "`basis/skills/reconcile-and-close/` exists
   and is empty".

   of its own" — UNVERIFIED, retract.** No research report on
   `origin/research` contains "checkout" (grep over all six); no notes
   file contains it; the two wordings also differ between F6 and item
   14. Fowler quotes the report does carry (F6, L422–424 and L437–443)
   say nothing about checkout. Required: delete the quote in both
   places; if item 14 needs a source for "stream-aligned for some
   flows", cite Fowler/Narayan "For initiatives that cut across multiple
   product-mode teams… solution champions" (report L437–440) or LeSS
   "feature team" (L451–453).

4. **F8 — `session-handoff` "each `hold-after: P7D`".** The
   `session-handoff.md` frontmatter (L1–11) has no `hold-after`;
   `hold-after: P7D` is on discovery-, review-, work-conversation, ICC,
   po-output-check, principle-set-authoring and research-inquiry.
   R2's obs. 14 made the error. Required: "the three conversation
   processes, each `hold-after: P7D`, plus `session-handoff`, all with
   classification enums (the three) and `bd` runtime steps".

5. **F8 — R3's "nineteen typedefs".** `grep -l '^type: artifact-typedef'
   basis/artifacts/*.md | wc -l` = 20 (all twenty files). Other counts
   check: 9 principles, 6 roles, 12 processes, 9 fitness sets, 11
   guidelines. Required: either correct to twenty with a note that R3
   counted nineteen, or mark the figure as the reader's count.

   `brief.md` (L32) and `acceptance-scenarios.md` (L39) require
   `framing`; `backlog-order.md` and `product-decision-record.md`
   Required-frontmatter sections do not name it. Required: "in two of
   the four PO typedefs (brief, acceptance scenarios)".

   item 7: the framing 'carries no status, measure, or history'" — that
   sentence is item 1 (L66–67). F6: "Product-process report F6: … 'nothing
   counts how often a request crosses contexts'" — that sentence is item
   7 (L143); F6 (L414–455) carries the LeSS quote but "component teams"
   as a label for context-owning teams is item 6 (L128–130), and the
   vocabulary note (L33–36). Required: cite item 1 in F3; in F6 cite
   item 6 for "component teams", item 7 for "nothing counts".

8. **F5 — R2's grep claim.** "grep for 'changelog|metric|measur' over
   `basis/` (excluding renderings) hits only principle statements and
   the designer's 'measured task completion'". A case-insensitive grep
   hits nine files: principles, experience-principles (L178, the
   designer standard), stakeholder-communication (L71 "measurable"),
   experience-record (L49, L82 "measured use"), decision-brief (L68
   "Budgets measured"), process-definition (history), lead-pm (L75),
   definition-chain-migration (L178 "by measure"). None is a product
   outcome measure, so the conclusion stands. Required: restate as "no
   hit names a measure of a shipped outcome; the nearest are lead-pm's
   evidence list, the designer's 'measured task completion', and the
   experience record's 'measured use'".

9. **F8 — "'definition chain — the six linked definitions' never
   enumerates the six".** The glossary entry (L55–56) does not, but
   `basis/types/definition-chain.md` L16–17 does: "typedef, guideline,
   fitness set, process, roles, skill". R3 wrote "never enumerated in
   the glossary" (notes-3 L106) and notes the type at L181. Required:
   "the glossary entry never enumerates the six; the list lives in
   `basis/types/definition-chain.md`, which nothing on the newcomer's
   path links".

10. **F9 — scope of the time-constant evidence.** "`hold-after: P7D` in
    the three conversation processes" is true but the constant is in
    seven processes (see 4); and "every loop returns to an `observe`
    step run by `product-authority`" holds only for the three
    conversation processes (`id: observe` at discovery L103, review
    L108, work L101; po-output-check and ICC loops have none). R1 wrote
    "every flow's loop" of those three. Required: "in seven processes;
    every conversation loop returns to…".

11. **Items 13 and Alternatives — "eleven definitions".** The proposal's
    item 9 (report L208–247) lists twelve bullets (two new typedefs,
    brief amend, lead-po, lead-pm, two fitness sets, architect,
    discovery, review, po-output-check, reconcile-and-close, three
    renderings). Required: "the dozen changes the proposal lists" or an
    explicit counting rule.

12. **Item 7 — "which the product-process report does and the basis
    does not".** The basis does state the same-person arrangement
    (`discovery-conversation.md` L37–39: "lead-pm — held by the same
    person") and the maker/checker split as po-output-check's purpose
    (history v1, L255); what it does not state is that the
    cold-reviewer screen is therefore the check of record. Required:
    narrow to "…the basis names the same-person holding but never says
    the screen is the check of record".

13. **Item 9 label — "(Medium; likely in use.)"** puts confidence and a
    likelihood word in one phrase, against the frame's rule ("stated
    separately"). Limitations also says "Predictions (items 9, 10) are
    labeled low" while item 9 is labeled medium. Required: label item 9
    "(Medium.)" with the likelihood in the body sentence ("for one
    person, the same as no prioritization process — likely"), or
    "(Medium; low on the prediction.)" as item 10 does; fix Limitations
    to match.

14. **Item 10 — "'one ask per step'".** Source: "A step returns at most
    one ask per run" (`process-definition.md` L99). Required: quote as
    written.

15. **Method — "noted by two readers".** Only notes-2 (obs. 0) records
    the `research`/`origin/research` lag; notes-1 and notes-3 contain no
    mention (grep for de72efa / remote / origin). Limitations repeats
    "two readers". Required: "noted by one reader".

16. **Method / summary — "the five research reports".** `origin/research`
    at `de72efa` holds six (`solutions-architect-role-2026-08.md`,
    commit b372e89, in addition to the five listed in Sources). The
    frame named five; the sixth was not read. Required: "the five
    research reports the frame named (a sixth, the solutions-architect
    report, was not opened)".

interviews the authority" (L425); primer opening (L3–4); core-tasks

"required before instances are authored or rewritten" — the draft's

default is the asker's (ask.md L46); research-prompting F1 on personas
(L71–75); every R-attributed phrase found verbatim in the notes.
